/mechanisms/1.name: Gluconobacter oxydans biolixiviant releases Nd from synthetic phosphate
/mechanisms/1.description: Biolixiviants produced by Gluconobacter oxydans B58 and its engineered derivatives solubilized Nd from synthetic Nd-phosphate powder. Selected transposon disruption strains changed filtered-leachate Nd concentrations relative to wild-type comparators. These observations do not identify a unique non-acid lixiviant or establish a recovered Nd product.
/mechanisms/1.context: Laboratory bench-scale validation used Mon2, a synthetic mixture of monazite-Nd and rhabdophane-Nd phases, not pure monazite or a natural ore. Living B58-derived cultures grown in yeast-peptone-mannitol medium were diluted with glucose to 20% w/v and incubated for 48 h at 30 degrees C and 200 rpm to produce biolixiviant. Mon2 was contacted at 1% pulp density for 24 h at 30 degrees C and 200 rpm. The method reports filtration after leaching through 0.45 micrometre filters, but does not specify cell removal before contact with Mon2. ICP-MS measured Nd in the filtrate. Three biological replicates were used per selected strain; wild-type, an intergenic-transposon proxy wild-type, and no-bacteria controls were prepared. Supplementary Data 4A reports final pH for the bacterial assays from 2.17 to 2.84; pH was an outcome rather than a fixed common treatment. The taxonomy identifier is species-level; B58 and its derivatives are specified by the study, not separately identified by that CURIE. The study demonstrates laboratory solubilization, not industrial operation.

evidence.explanation: Results describing Mon2, Fig. 3, and Methods, Direct REE-bioleaching measurements, support the substrate, controls and Nd assay. Eight of twelve selected disruption strains increased extraction by 56-111% relative to proxy wild-type; these are relative improvements, not percentages of the substrate Nd recovered. No-bacteria controls are described in Methods but are not included in Supplementary Data 4A's 42 bacterial observations, limiting independent reconstruction of background-corrected absolute dissolution from that workbook alone.

Sheet 4A contains three observations for each of twelve selected disruption strains, WT and pWT B, with extraction, final pH and final optical density. The pWT B and delta-GO_1598 triplicates support the reported approximately 111% relative improvement. Absolute workbook extraction values are not converted to a percent yield here.

Figs. 3-5 and Discussion preserve limits on genetic and chemical causality: a GO_1096 transposon disruption strongly decreased extraction, but its clean deletion did not reproduce that effect. Nine of twelve selected mutants did not significantly change pH relative to proxy wild-type; this suggests additional contributions but does not identify a chelator, redox compound or single causal pathway. Synthetic mixed-phase results are not evidence for equivalent performance on natural monazite or Nd-bearing waste.

/sources/5.title: Marecos et al. (2025). Direct genome-scale screening of Gluconobacter oxydans B58 for rare earth element bioleaching. Communications Biology 8:682.
